about.title: Loomis Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Loomis residents rely on nearby Placer County clinics, urgent care centers, and Sacramento-area hospitals for everything from routine visits to surgical care. Most of the time, that care goes as expected. But when a diagnosis is missed, a medication is mismanaged, or a surgical error occurs, the effects can upend a family's daily life in a town of just under 7,000 people, where everyone seems to know everyone. California's medical malpractice rules are notably strict, with tight filing windows and specific notice requirements that differ from ordinary injury claims. A bad medical result by itself doesn't necessarily mean malpractice occurred — proving a case requires qualified expert review and careful documentation. We review the details of what happened and explain your options based on California law. There's no obligation, and if we take your case, you don't pay unless there's a recovery.

items.title: We Understand MICRA's Tight Deadlines
items.desc: California generally requires malpractice claims within one year of discovering the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself. We help make sure your Loomis claim isn't lost to a missed deadline.

items.title: We Know the 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before filing suit, California law typically requires giving the healthcare provider 90 days' advance notice. Missing this step can delay or derail a claim, so early attorney involvement matters.

items.title: We Work With Qualified Medical Experts
items.desc: Because a poor outcome alone isn't proof of malpractice, cases almost always need a qualified medical expert to establish what went wrong. We work with such experts to build a supported case.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice claim in Loomis?
items.answer: Under California's MICRA rules, you generally have one year from when you discover the injury, but never more than three years from the date it occurred. These deadlines are strict and vary based on your specific facts, so it's worth having us review your timeline as soon as possible.

items.question: Is there a cap on what I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: Yes, California law places a cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in medical malpractice cases, though that cap rises each year under current law. Economic damages, such as medical bills and lost income, are generally not subject to this cap. We can explain how this applies to your situation.

items.question: My family sees doctors near Sierra College Boulevard and Taylor Road — does location matter for my claim?
items.answer: Where you received care in the Loomis area doesn't change California's malpractice laws, but it can affect which court has jurisdiction and which records need to be gathered. We can sort out these details once we understand where and how your treatment took place.

items.question: Does a bad medical outcome automatically mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that medicine involves uncertainty, so a poor result alone isn't enough to prove malpractice. A qualified medical expert typically needs to review the case and confirm the care fell below the accepted standard.
